definitions.explanation: The ability to do something skillfully, smoothly, and efficiently. Refers to how well and quickly one handles tasks, especially practical or manual ones.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{手際|てぎわ}よく{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: She cooked the meal skillfully and efficiently.

examples.japanese: {手際|てぎわ}が{悪|わる}くて、{時間|じかん}がかかってしまった。
examples.english: I was inefficient and it took too long.

examples.japanese: {手際|てぎわ}のいい{仕事|しごと}ぶりに{感心|かんしん}した。
examples.english: I was impressed by the skillful way the work was done.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{手際|てぎわ}がいい/よい (skillful, efficient, deft)
・{手際|てぎわ}が{悪|わる}い (clumsy, inefficient)
・{手際|てぎわ}よく (skillfully, efficiently - adverb)
・{鮮|あざ}やかな{手際|てぎわ} (brilliant/impressive skill)

USAGE:
{手際|てぎわ} emphasizes smooth, efficient execution—doing something without wasted motion or time.
・{手際|てぎわ}よく{片付|かたづ}ける (to clean up efficiently)
・{手際|てぎわ}よく{仕事|しごと}をこなす (to handle work efficiently)

CONTEXT:
Often used for cooking, housework, crafts, and any practical tasks where efficiency and skill are valued.

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
・{手|て} (hand) + {際|ぎわ} (edge/skill) = skill with the hands

RELATED WORDS:
・{腕前|うでまえ} (skill, ability - more about capability level)
・{手|て}さばき (dexterity, handling skill - especially with tools/objects)
